items.title: How one optimal AUKUS submarine pathway became two
items.description: Scrutiny of AUKUS's delivery reveals two "optimal pathways" for Australia's submarines.

items.title: ABS estimates 80pc of tobacco consumed in Australia last year was illegally sourced
items.description: The experimental estimates are based on "nicotine metabolite concentrations" detected in wastewater samples, combined with data showing a collapse in spending on legal cigarettes and vapes.

items.title: Another KPMG leader steps aside amid audit leak scandal fallout
items.description: KPMG Australia chief operating officer Eileen Hoggett will step aside from her role while investigations are pending into the audit leak scandal at the big four firm.

items.title: Parents of fit 27-year-old asked what quality of life he had by medical staff
items.description: Sam Stubbs’s parents were asked about his quality of life while treating him for a lung infection. They realised it was because he was born with Down syndrome.

items.title: 'Too dangerous to push ahead': Aussie diver leaves Laos cave rescue
items.description: Josh Richards is on his way back to Australia, after multiple days helping rescue miners trapped in a Laos cave.

items.title: Neo-Nazi Thomas Sewell broadcasting hate on Instagram from Victorian acreage
items.description: ABC NEWS Verify can reveal that Neo-Nazi leader Thomas Sewell has been uploading antisemitic and homophobic diatribes to Instagram from a property on the outskirts of Melbourne.

items.title: Defence plans to sell Sydney Harbour land Albanese once fought to protect
items.description: Parliamentary speeches from 2021 reveal the prime minister was opposed to privatising Sydney Harbour land now being sold off by the Defence Department.

items.title: Bolivia's defense minister resigns amid weeks of mass protests

featured_image.name: Bolivia's defence minister resigns after weeks of mass protests | Reuters

items.description: Bolivia's Defense Minister Marcelo Salinas resigned on Tuesday after a month of anti-government protests that have blocked roads and cut off access to major cities, a ministry source confirmed to Reuters. The departure marks the highest-level exit from President Rodrigo Paz's government since unrest engulfed the country in early May.[1][2]

items.title: These are the 'worst offenders' in Australian packaging
items.description: A trendy plastic-and-metal takeaway cup used by cafes for iced drinks has been named Australia's worst packaging in the first Unpackit Awards.

items.title: Trump endorses Colombia presidential candidate De La Espriella

featured_image.name: Right-wing candidate pulls ahead in Colombia's presidential vote

items.description: U.S. President Donald Trump on Tuesday endorsed Abelardo De La Espriella, a right-wing lawyer seeking Colombia's presidency, inserting himself into a polarized Latin American contest ahead of a June 21 runoff election. Trump posted on Truth Social that the outcome of the vote "is crucial for the future of Colombia and its ties with the United States," according to Reuters.[1][2]

items.title: New Solomon Islands leader wants to 'reset' relations with Australia
items.description: The new Solomon Islands PM has made a clear pivot towards Australia, agreeing to kickstart negotiations on a comprehensive treaty and promising to "review" the Pacific nation's contentious security agreement with China.

items.title: Australia's economy growing at 2.5 per cent annually as slowdown begins
items.description: Australia's economy grew at an annual rate of 2.5 per cent in the March quarter, the same as in the previous quarter.

items.title: IRGC strikes US Fifth Fleet headquarters in Bahrain

featured_image.name: Iran's IRGC attacks US Fifth Fleet headquarters, airbase, local media  reports | Reuters

items.description:
Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps launched missile and drone attacks on the U.S. Fifth Fleet headquarters in Bahrain and an airbase in a neighboring country on Tuesday, in what Tehran described as retaliation for American strikes on a communications tower south of Qeshm Island, according to Reuters and Iranian state media.[1][2]

The IRGC's naval forces also targeted a vessel identified as the Panaya with missiles, claiming the strike was a response to a U.S. attack on an Iranian tanker near the Strait of Hormuz that allegedly damaged the ship's engine room. "Endangering the security of the Strait of Hormuz will result in significant repercussions for the U.S. military," the IRGC said, according to Iranian media.[3][1]

items.title: Rubio says Netanyahu's plan to seize 70% of Gaza contradicts US vision

featured_image.name: Rubio says Netanyahu's goal to seize 70% of Gaza contradicts ...

items.description:
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's directive to expand military control over the Gaza Strip to 70% has drawn a rare public rebuke from the Trump administration, with Secretary of State Marco Rubio telling lawmakers on Tuesday that the plan contradicts the U.S. vision for the territory.

"We have a plan. It doesn't call for that," Rubio said during congressional testimony when pressed on Netanyahu's announcement, according to Anadolu Agency. The remarks, made during back-to-back hearings on Capitol Hill, represent one of the clearest signals of daylight between Washington and Jerusalem on Gaza policy.[1][2][3]

items.title: US fires Hellfire missile at tanker heading to Iran

featured_image.name: US blockade: Missile cripples crude oil tanker M/T Lexie, preventing it  from reaching Iran's Kharg Island

items.description:
U.S. Central Command announced Tuesday that a U.S. aircraft fired a Hellfire missile into the engine room of the Botswana-flagged tanker M/T Lexie after its crew ignored repeated warnings over a 24-hour period while transiting international waters toward Iran's Kharg Island oil terminal.[1][2]

The strike marks the sixth commercial vessel disabled since CENTCOM began enforcing its naval blockade of Iranian ports on April 13, with U.S. forces having redirected 122 other ships attempting to enter or exit Iranian ports during that period.[1]

items.title: Kuwait condemns 'repeated' Iranian missile and drone attacks on its territory

featured_image.name: Kuwait condemns Iranian attacks on its territory as flagrant violation of  sovereignty, security

items.description:
Kuwait's Cabinet on Tuesday issued a strong condemnation of what it called "repeated Iranian missile and drone attacks" targeting Kuwaiti territory, describing the strikes as dangerous provocations and affirming the country's full right to defend its sovereignty.[2]

The statement followed two separate incidents — the first on Friday, May 29, when Kuwaiti air defenses responded to missile and drone strikes following US operations against Iranian drones, and a second on Monday, June 1, when Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) launched missiles targeting US forces stationed in Kuwait.[3][2]

items.title: Kremlin demands Ukraine cede territory hours after deadly mass attack

featured_image.name: Russia launches massive drone and missile attack on Ukraine, killing 3 in  Kyiv - OPB

items.description: Hours after Russia unleashed one of the largest aerial attacks of its full-scale invasion, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov declared on Tuesday that the war could end within 24 hours if Ukrainian forces withdrew from Donbas and other Russian-occupied territories. Ukrainian media outlet NV described the statement as a "cynical ultimatum," noting its timing in the wake of strikes that killed dozens of civilians across Ukraine.[1]

items.title: UNICEF says Iran war delaying lifesaving aid for children

featured_image.name: Iran war disruption threatening delivery of lifesaving supplies for children,  UN says | Reuters

items.description: The United Nations children's agency warned on Tuesday that surging global transport costs and supply chain disruptions linked to the war in Iran are threatening the delivery of lifesaving aid to children worldwide, with some shipments delayed by up to six months.

items.title: Bahrain bans citizens from traveling to Iran and Iraq

featured_image.name: Bahrain bans citizens from traveling to Iraq, Iran over 'tense security  situation'

items.description: Bahrain's Interior Ministry on Tuesday banned citizens from traveling to Iran and Iraq until further notice, citing "continued security tensions" in the region. The decision comes as the Shiite Muslim holy month of Muharram approaches, during which millions of Shiites traditionally travel to Karbala in Iraq for pilgrimage.[1][2][3]

items.title: Russia kills at least 17 in massive overnight barrage on Ukraine

featured_image.name: Kyiv comes under intense air attack

items.description:
Russia launched one of the largest combined aerial attacks of its full-scale war against Ukraine overnight into Tuesday, firing 73 missiles and 656 drones at cities across the country, killing at least 13 people and wounding more than 100, Ukrainian officials said.[1][2][3]

The assault, which began Monday evening, targeted Kyiv, the central city of Dnipro, Kharkiv, and other areas including Poltava and Zaporizhzhia, according to Ukraine's air force. Ukrainian air defenses intercepted 40 missiles and 602 drones during the onslaught.[4][5][6]

items.title: President Trump Announces U.S. Military Airstrike in Venezuela
items.description: President Trump states the U.S. military conducted its first known airstrike inside Venezuela targeting a dock where drugs were allegedly loaded onto boats[1][2][4].

items.title: Trump Meets Netanyahu at Mar-a-Lago for Gaza Ceasefire Phase Two Talks
items.description: President Trump met with Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu to discuss advancing phase two of the Gaza ceasefire, including reconstruction and responses to Iran[1][4].

items.title: Feds Launch Massive Taxpayer Fraud Probe in Minnesota After Viral Video
items.description: Federal agencies including DHS, FBI, and ICE investigate $110 million in suspected fraud at Minnesota child care centers following a viral YouTube video[3].

items.title: Americans Express Widespread Opposition to AI Data Centers
items.description: Public backlash against AI infrastructure data centers grows, with protests and demands for bans influencing Democratic Party strategies for future elections[3].

items.title: Elon Musk's Humanoid Robot Vision: China Poised to Lead Production
items.description: China prioritizes humanoid robots in tech race with U.S., ramping up production while warning of industry bubble and potential bottlenecks[3].

items.description: President Trump spoke with Putin amid ongoing Ukraine conflict, with Russia reevaluating peace plan tenets after Ukrainian denials[1].

items.description: Seven Democrats vying for Wisconsin governor blame economic issues on Trump and emphasize affordability ahead of 2026 primary[3].
